📰 Why can Uniswap’s aggregator hooks operate across three chains at once?

Uniswap Labs has officially launched aggregator hooks, allowing Uniswap v4 to route trades through liquidity held on external platforms. This means users can trade on emerging chains such as Base and Robinhood Chain, not just Ethereum. This has far-reaching implications for the entire DeFi ecosystem and users’ cross-chain experience.

Why does this news matter?
At its core, the aggregator hook is Uniswap’s attempt to break out of its own liquidity silos, driven by several deeper factors. First, although Uniswap v4 offers improved performance, liquidity continues to flow out, while competitors such as SushiSwap and Aave are actively expanding across multiple chains. Second, Ethereum’s high fees and congestion are pushing users and capital toward lower-cost chains, and Uniswap wants to keep users within its ecosystem through hooks. Finally, this signals DeFi’s move toward compliant partnerships amid regulatory pressure—using officially recognized aggregators for cross-chain activity is safer than operating in a fully decentralized manner.

What does this mean for the market landscape? Uniswap isn’t simply adding a feature this time; it’s using hooks to build a liquidity network, much like a clearinghouse in traditional finance. This could improve capital efficiency and squeeze arbitrage opportunities. It may boost short-term sentiment toward ETH and BTC, but in the long run, it will intensify competition across the ecosystem. Historically, only a few similar innovations have become industry standards. For example, as with the early days of the Lightning Network, most attempts ultimately became niche tools.

Market impact
The most direct impact on BTC and ETH is lower trading costs. For example, when trading ETH on Base, Uniswap hooks can tap directly into Ethereum’s vast liquidity pools, potentially bringing fees down to just one-tenth of those charged by traditional cross-chain bridges. In the short term, ETH could see a sentiment-driven rise within hours of hook-enabled chains gaining traction, but the medium-term outlook depends on whether these chains can actually attract large-scale capital. Historical data shows that new DeFi features only become trends when they solve real problems, as Compound’s high interest rates did in its early days.

The impact on the regulatory environment is even greater. Aggregators offer an auditable cross-chain solution, making it easier for regulators to track the flow of funds. This means that as agencies such as the CFTC and SEC keep a close eye on DeFi, Uniswap’s hooks could become a new industry model and compel other projects to follow suit with compliance measures. Data on capital flows shows that when DeFi tools gain regulatory acceptance, the tokens associated with them often attract institutional investment.

Trading strategy
💡 Uniswap aggregator hooks are more valuable for ETH’s long-term prospects than as a short-term price catalyst, although ETH could rise by $200–$300 in the near term on hype around its practical utility. This view is invalidated if future data shows that total value locked (TVL) on hook-enabled chains falls short of expectations.

📰 为什么Uniswap聚合器钩子能同时跑三条链？

Uniswap Labs正式上线聚合器钩子，让Uniswap v4可以经由外部平台持有的流动性进行交易路由。这意味着用户可以通过Base、Robinhood Chain等新兴链交易，而不只是Ethereum。这对整个DeFi生态和用户跨链体验产生深远影响。

为什么这条新闻重要？
聚合器钩子的本质是Uniswap试图打破自身流动性孤岛，这是由几个深层逻辑驱动的。首先，Uniswap v4虽然性能提升但流动性持续外流，竞争对手如SushiSwap和Aave都在积极布局多链。其次，Ethereum的高费用和拥堵让用户和资金流向成本更低的链，Uniswap想通过钩子把用户留在其生态中。最后，这是监管压力下DeFi走向合规合作的信号——通过官方认可的聚合器实现跨链，比完全去中心化操作更安全。

对市场格局意味着什么？Uniswap这次不是简单加个功能，而是用钩子构建了一个流动性网络，就像传统金融的清算所。这意味着资金效率提升、套利空间被压缩，对ETH和BTC的短期情绪可能有提振，但长期看是生态竞争的白热化。历史上类似事件只有少数能成为行业标准，比如闪电网络早期，多数尝试最后都沦为边缘化工具。

对市场的影响
对BTC/ETH最直接的影响是交易成本下降。比如ETH在Base链上交易，通过Uniswap钩子可以直接利用Ethereum庞大的流动性池，费用可能只有传统跨链桥的十分之一。短期内看，ETH可能在钩子链普及的几个小时内获得情绪性上涨，但中期取决于这些链能否真正吸引到大规模资金。历史数据表明，DeFi新功能只有当它解决了实际问题时才能转化为趋势（比如早期 Compound 的高利率）。

对监管环境的影响更大。聚合器是一种可审计的跨链方案，让监管机构更容易追踪资金流向。这意味着在CFTC和SEC等机构紧盯DeFi的背景下，Uniswap的钩子可能成为行业新范式，迫使其他项目跟进合规。资金流向数据显示，当DeFi工具被监管接受时，相关代币往往能获得机构资金入场。

操作思路
💡 Uniswap聚合器钩子对ETH的长期价值大于短期价格刺激，但短期内ETH可能因实用主义炒作上涨200-300美元。如果未来数据显示钩子链上的总价值锁仓(TVL)低于预期，这个判断作废。

The Square has recently banned a batch of accounts. Here are some patterns I’ve noticed.

1518 Principal has been permanently banned. A number of accounts that grew rapidly have also gradually had their reach restricted or been banned.

This isn’t the first time, and it won’t be the last.

I’ve been on the Square for 5.7 years. I’ve seen too many schemes, and witnessed the platform go from turning a blind eye to seriously enforcing its rules.

Here’s a summary of some common paths to violating the rules, as a heads-up for those still making content in good faith:

━━ Scheme 1: Rapid account growth + luring people into buying at the top ━━
The playbook: Post a lot of content in a short time → build a following → lure people into buying at the top → disappear.
Signs: An unusually high posting frequency, highly repetitive content, and comments directing people to add them on WeChat or Telegram.
How the platform detects it: Abnormal account activity + user reports + manual review.
Outcome: The account gets banned. Directing users off-platform crosses a clear line in the rules.

━━ Scheme 2: Vote manipulation and buying votes ━━
Paying people to vote during an event to boost your ranking with your follower count.
The platform is extremely strict about this—this year’s event rules clearly prohibit any form of paid engagement.
It’s not a reach restriction; it’s a permanent ban, with no grace period.

━━ Scheme 3: Switching to a new account after a ban ━━
Thinking you can start over just by changing accounts.
In reality, the platform can link accounts through the same IP address, device, phone number, or similar content style.
The community guidelines are clear: registering a new account and continuing the same activity after being penalized is itself a violation, and can easily lead to the new account being penalized too.

━━ Scheme 4: Redirecting people off-platform ━━
Directing users to contact you through a third party, moving them to a “safe place” to fleece them.
The rules for the Square spell out this red line very clearly, and the success rate for appeals is extremely low.

━━ One question worth considering ━━

Why do these accounts do this?

Because the short-term gains are too high and the cost of breaking the rules is too low—until now.

The platform has started a systematic cleanup. These aren’t random spot checks; they’re data-driven, large-scale reviews. Accounts aren’t being banned because they got unlucky—they crossed a threshold the system is designed to detect.

广场最近封了一批号。说说我观察到的规律。

1518校长永封了。还有一批快速起号的账号陆续被限流、封禁。

这不是第一次，也不会是最后一次。

我在广场做了5.7年。见过太多套路，也见证了平台从睁一眼闭一眼到开始认真执法的全过程。

总结一下常见的违规路径，给还在认真做内容的人提个醒：

━━ 套路一：快速起号+高位引导接盘━━
逻辑：短期内发大量内容→积累粉丝→引导高位接盘→消失。
特征：发帖频率异常高，内容高度雷同，评论区引导加微信/Telegram。
平台识别方式：账号行为异常+用户举报+人工复核。
结果：账号封禁，导流行为直接触发规则红线。

━━ 套路二：投票刷票买票 ━━
活动期间找人有偿投票，以粉丝量换取排名。
平台对此极为敏感——今年活动规则明确禁止任何形式的有偿互动。
不是限流，是永封，没有缓冲期。

━━ 套路三：封号后换新号 ━━
以为换个号就能重来。
实际上：同IP、同设备、同手机号、相似内容风格，平台有能力关联。
社区准则明确：被处罚后注册新号继续活动本身就是违规，容易被连坐处理。

━━ 套路四：转引站外 ━━
引导用户去第三方联系，转移到「安全地带」收割。
这条红线在广场条款里写得很清楚，且申诉成功率极低。

━━ 一个问题值得思考 ━━

为什么这些账号做这些事？

因为短期收益太高，违规成本太低——直到现在。

平台开始系统性清理，不是随机抽查，是数据驱动的批量审核。被封的不是运气差，是触碰了系统识别的阈值。

认真做内容的人，这是好消息。
噪音少了，算法给真内容的流量才会变多。

广场正在完成一次自我净化。

ETH funds currently show $4.4 million in net inflows | Key figures still unreported | I won’t chase an early long

I’m still cautious and waiting. An ETF table that hasn’t been fully populated is not evidence that capital is flowing back across the board. As of the time of writing, Farside shows that among the reported U.S. spot Ethereum fund figures for October 23, FETH saw inflows of $3.6 million and MSSE saw inflows of $800,000, for a current automatically calculated total of $4.4 million. But ETHA, ETHB, and ETHV are still marked with dashes. A dash means data is not yet available; it does not mean zero. The full row for the previous day, October 22, showed net outflows of $110.6 million. The two days’ figures also cannot be directly compared when disclosure is incomplete to different degrees, much less used to claim that ETH funds have already shifted from outflows to net inflows.

The mechanism by which this affects the crypto market is straightforward: fund creations and redemptions ultimately feed through issuance, market-making, and custody channels into ETH exposure. Sustained net inflows could bring stable demand to the spot market; positive figures from a handful of funds cannot prove that overall buying is sufficient to absorb selling through other channels. Ethereum products also differ in structure: some offer staking rewards, while others do not. BlackRock’s ETHB issuer materials state that it tracks the price of ETH and seeks to share staking rewards; its fees, operations, and staking risks still need to be considered separately. A fund’s existence or staking feature does not mean it buys additional ETH every day, nor does it mean holders receive a fixed return. Product design and daily flows should not be bundled together into a bullish slogan.

The market has not yet confirmed the optimistic narrative through price action either. At the time of writing, Kraken ETH/USD was around $2,377, below the day’s open of about $2,385, with a rolling 24-hour low of around $2,350 and a high of around $2,415. Binance News noted strong demand for short-term protection in Ethereum options. This is an observation about risk appetite in derivatives, not a prediction that spot prices must fall. My key levels are the intraday low area around $2,350, the opening level near $2,385, and the upper confirmation zone at $2,415. A recovery would only have a basis if ETH regains and holds above $2,385 and the combined ETF flows remain positive after the missing major figures are reported. If it falls below $2,350 and fails to reclaim it on a bounce, the short-term stabilization thesis is invalidated. If it breaks above $2,415 but immediately falls back below, beware of a false breakout.

If I were trading this myself, I wouldn’t chase a rally now. I’d only consider a small spot long if specific conditions are met. I’d wait for ETH to hold above $2,385 and successfully retest that level, while the ETF data is filled in and does not turn into a significant net outflow. Only then would I enter with no more than 2.5% of my total capital. I’d take half off at the first target of $2,415 and hold the rest toward $2,460. After entry, I’d stop out if ETH falls below $2,350. I’d also close the remaining position if fund flows reverse sharply, a project upgrade introduces new unresolved risks, or the daily close falls below the opening level. If the signal doesn’t appear, I stay out. For me, missing one trade is better than treating unconfirmed information as certainty.

ETH基金暂现440万美元净流入｜关键大项未报｜我不追先手多

我的态度仍是谨慎等待，不能把一张尚未填完的ETF表当成资金全面回流的证据。Farside截至写稿显示，10月23日美国现货以太坊基金已报项目里，FETH流入360万美元、MSSE流入80万美元，自动合计暂为440万美元；但ETHA、ETHB以及ETHV仍是横杠。横杠代表尚无可用数据，不等于零。前一日10月22日整行显示净流出1.106亿美元，两天数字也不能在披露完整度不同的时候直接比较，更不能说ETH资金已经从流出转为净流入。

这件事影响加密市场的机制不复杂：基金申赎最终要通过发行、做市及托管链条反映到ETH敞口，持续净流入才可能为现货带来稳定需求；零星几只基金的正数，无法证明整体买盘足以覆盖其他渠道的卖盘。尤其以太坊产品之间结构不同，有的带质押收益，有的没有。贝莱德ETHB发行方资料写明其追踪ETH价格并寻求分享质押奖励，费用、运营和质押风险仍需单独看。基金存在或提供质押功能，不代表每天都在新增ETH，也不等于持有人拥有固定收益。不能把基金产品设计和每日流量混成一个利多口号。

市场目前也没有用价格确认乐观叙事。Kraken ETH/USD写稿约2377美元，低于当日开盘约2385美元，滚动24小时低点约2350美元、高点约2415美元。Binance News提到以太坊短期期权保护需求偏强，这只是衍生品风险偏好的观察，不是现货必跌的预言。我的关键位是2350美元的日内低区、2385美元附近的开盘位及2415美元的上方验证区。若重新站稳2385美元且主要ETF缺失数据补齐后合计仍为净流入，才具备谈修复的基础；若失守2350美元并反抽不过，短线企稳判断就被推翻。若突破2415美元却马上跌回，也要防止假突破。

如果是我自己交易，现在不参与追涨，方向只预设条件触发后的现货轻仓多。等ETH在2385美元上方维持并回踩不破，同时ETF数据补齐且不转成明显净流出，才以总资金最多2.5%入场；第一目标2415美元减半，余仓看2460美元。入场后若跌破2350美元则止损，若基金数据大幅逆转、项目升级出现新增未解决风险，或价格收盘失守开盘位，就平掉余仓。信号没出现就是空仓；对我来说，少做一次也好过把未确认的信息交易成确定性。

title: 逐仓和全仓有什么区别？新手该用哪个？
subTitle:
开合约时会让你选「逐仓」或「全仓」，很多新手随手一点，结果吃了大亏。

【全仓】账户里所有余额都作为保证金。优点：强平价远，不容易被打爆；
缺点：一旦行情极端，亏损可能吃掉你整个账户。它是把所有鸡蛋放在一个
篮子里互相撑着。

【逐仓】只把指定的一笔钱分配给这个仓位。这个仓爆了，最多亏这一份，
不会传染到其他仓位和本金。风险被装进了笼子里。

【我的建议】新手一律逐仓。原因很简单：你还没有能力评估「一笔错单最坏
亏多少」，那就用制度帮你锁定最大损失。等你学会了仓位管理、连续三
个月稳定盈利，再考虑全仓也来得及。市场里活得久，比赚得快重要一百倍。

translatedData.title: What’s the difference between isolated and cross margin? Which should beginners use?
translatedData.subTitle:
When opening a futures contract, you’ll be asked to choose “isolated margin” or “cross margin.” Many beginners tap one without thinking and end up taking a big loss.

[Cross margin] All the balance in your account is used as margin. Advantage: the liquidation price is farther away, so you’re less likely to get liquidated;
Disadvantage: in extreme market conditions, losses could wipe out your entire account. It’s like putting all your eggs in one
They support each other in the same basket.

[Isolated margin] Only a specified amount of money is allocated to this position. If this position gets liquidated, you can lose at most that amount,
and the loss won’t spread to your other positions or principal. The risk is kept in a cage.

translatedData.content:
The options market is buying insurance against a drop, while the leveraged market won’t pay a cent in premiums—and the most important thing to read in today’s ETH dashboard isn’t that -0.53%.

First, look at the options signal itself. Put demand is at its strongest since early October, yet the price is down just 0.53%, with 24-hour trading volume of 5.91 billion USDT. This combination suggests that buyers of protection aren’t betting on direction: if they were, both price and funding rates would weaken, rather than only the volatility surface moving. Buying protection looks more like hedging—people already holding spot or bullish exposure are paying a premium amid uncertainty, rather than exiting their positions. That’s the difference between insurance and a bet: a bet leaves its mark on the candlestick chart; insurance leaves its mark on the volatility surface. Today, only the latter is moving.

The second dimension is funding rates, where the real disconnect lies. Perpetual funding is +0.0022%/8h, or less than 2.5% annualized—basically zero. But open interest stands at 5.517 billion USDT, and 76.0% of accounts are long. Put those two figures together and it gets interesting: three-quarters of accounts are long, yet funding barely moves. That means that when weighted by notional value, longs have no meaningful upper hand. In other words, small accounts are carrying the longs, while large players are neither chasing longs in perpetuals nor willing to pay to hold them—and the big money buying puts is probably that same group. So today’s structure isn’t “market panic”; it’s big money buying insurance while small money runs naked. Two groups are pricing the same risk in completely different ways, and no one is willing to pay a premium for it on the leverage side.

The third dimension is why fundamentals are absent from the picture. Seven-day mainnet revenue is down 18% to $2.16 million. This has been treated as a side note, but it explains exactly why risk is being bought through options rather than expressed by selling spot: ETH currently has no fee-driven narrative of its own to anchor pricing power, so marginal pricing is being driven by macro liquidity and leverage positioning. In this environment, the rational response to uncertainty is to hedge, not exit—exiting means giving up beta; hedging costs only the premium.

Watch three things next, in this order:

First, whether puts are being rolled or exercised. If implied volatility rises while spot stays flat, that means premiums are continuing to burn, and these hedges will eventually be closed—potentially turning into forced buying. If IV falls while spot weakens, that’s when hedging has turned into a directional bet.

Second, whether funding turns negative. Negative funding means shorts are starting to pay to bet on a drop, shifting the dynamic from “buying insurance” to “betting on direction.” At that point, a 0.53% decline will be nowhere near enough to tell the story. As long as funding sits near zero, even aggressive put buying is just insurance.

Third, whether the 76% share of long accounts acts as a buffer or fuel while the market moves sideways. If funding stays flat and prices drift lower, unrealized losses on these accounts will build and trigger forced position reductions—that’s a slow bleed, not a wick, and the two require completely different responses.

My read is that this dashboard is pricing in “moderate downside with tail protection”—neither a crash scenario nor anything healthy. The real switch is funding: as long as it stays near zero, even strong put demand is just insurance; if it breaks below zero, those same puts can shift from hedges into accelerants. The risk in the positioning structure isn’t the direction itself, but that when these protections expire or are closed, the market could lose both its buffer and its source of buying demand at the same time.

#ETH #Ethereum #Crypto

content:
期权市场在给下跌买保险，杠杆市场一分保费都不肯出——今天 ETH 这张表最该读的，不是那 -0.53%。

先看期权这个信号本身。Put 需求创 10 月初以来最强，但价格只跌了 0.53%，24 小时成交 59.1 亿 USDT。这个组合说明买保护的人不是来押方向的：真要押方向，价格和费率会一起走弱，而不是只有曲面在动。买保护的动作更像对冲——手上本来就有现货或看多敞口，遇到不确定先付保费，而不是清仓。保险和赌注的区别就在这里：赌注只会在 K 线上留下痕迹，保险只在波动率曲面上留下痕迹，而今天只有后者在动。

第二个维度是费率，这才是真正的错位。永续费率 +0.0022%/8h，年化不到 2.5%，基本等于零。但持仓量有 55.17 亿 USDT，多头账户占比 76.0%。两个数字放一起就有意思了：账户层面四分之三在做多，费率却几乎不动，说明按名义金额加权后，多头完全不占上风。换句话说，这边扛多的是小额账户，大额资金既不在永续追多，也不愿意为多付钱——那批买 put 的，很可能就是这批大钱。所以今天的结构不是“市场恐慌”，而是大钱买保险、小钱裸奔。同一个风险，两拨人在用完全不同的方式定价，且没人愿意在杠杆端为它付溢价。

第三个维度是基本面为什么缺位。主网 7 日收入下滑 18% 到 216 万美元，这条被当成花边，但它恰好解释了为什么风险被买在期权而不是砸在现货：ETH 眼下没有自己的费用叙事能接住定价权，边际定价落在宏观流动性和杠杆结构上。在这种状态下，遇到不确定，理性动作是对冲而非离场——离场等于放弃 beta，对冲只损失保费。

接下来盯三件事，顺序别搞反：

一是 put 是滚动还是被行使。如果隐含波动率抬升而现货不动，说明保费在持续烧钱，这批对冲最终会平仓，那反而会变成被动买盘；如果 IV 回落同时现货走弱，那才是对冲变成了方向。

二是费率会不会转负。费率翻负意味着空头开始为下跌付费，性质就从“买保险”变成“押方向”，那时候 0.53% 这个跌幅根本不够看。费率躺在零附近，put 买得再凶也只是保险。

三是 76% 的多头账户占比在横盘里是缓冲还是燃料。如果费率不动、价格缓跌，这批账户的浮亏会累积并触发被动减仓——那是慢速出血的形态，不是插针，两者的处理方式完全不同。

我的判断是：这张表定价的是“温和下行加尾部保护”，既不是崩盘定价，也谈不上健康。真正的开关在费率上——它待在零附近，看跌期权再强也只是保险；它一旦向下破零，同一批期权会从对冲变成加速器。仓位结构上的风险不在方向，而在于这批保护到期或平仓时，市场同时失去缓冲和买盘。

① 守住80402，贴地爬行等修复，上方先看81219，收不回去一切白搭。
② 跌破80402，隔夜低点80461形同虚设，下方空间打开，别急着问支撑在哪。

唯一硬气的是BNB：逆势涨0.67%报736，上方750。别人跳水它慢跑，独立行情。

📰 A Vast ETF Funding Gap: Why Is Bitcoin 100 Times Stronger Than Ethereum?

Bitcoin ETFs attracted a whopping $525 million in a single day recently, while Ethereum ETFs brought in just $14 million. This shows a marked divergence in the market’s choice between Bitcoin and Ethereum, and may signal a long-term shift in cryptocurrency investment strategies.

Why does this news matter?
It reflects investors’ growing confidence in Bitcoin’s value. The huge inflows into Bitcoin ETFs suggest that the market increasingly sees Bitcoin as a safer safe-haven asset, while the weakness of Ethereum ETFs highlights uncertainty around its regulatory outlook and future roadmap. This divergence comes as regulators advance approval processes for both types of ETFs, meaning Bitcoin has already taken an early lead in gaining acceptance in traditional finance.

Market impact
In the short term, direct support from ETF inflows could give Bitcoin a price advantage, while Ethereum may need technological breakthroughs or new use cases to attract capital. Over the long term, if this divergence continues, it could reshape how cryptocurrencies are valued: Bitcoin may come to resemble gold, while Ethereum may be more like a tech stock. Deposits in DeFi lending pools have recently taken off, surging from $4B at the start of the year to more than $10B. Stablecoins don’t face the same strict constraints as Bitcoin, and can offer better returns, so it’s only natural that money is flowing into DeFi lending pools. What does $10B in deposits mean? Impact on the market
In the short term, this is likely to put pressure on BTC and ETH. Large institutional allocations often go hand in hand with market volatility. Rising lending rates in particular can attract arbitrage capital and push ETH higher, but for a broader macro asset like BTC, they’re more a signal of where capital is flowing—and a short-term negative. What about the long term? If this model proves viable, continued institutional participation could bring healthier capital flows to the entire on-chain ecosystem. More realistically, though, regulators may soon get involved. After all, when this much money is pooled together, who takes responsibility if something goes wrong? What does this mean? Institutional participation is a double-edged sword: on one hand, it supports demand; on the other, it amplifies compliance risks.

📰 Why has the OCC’s GENIUS rule suddenly upset banking associations?

The American Bankers Association (ABA) has suddenly come out against the OCC’s new stablecoin rule, GENIUS, focusing mainly on changes to the provisions on yield. In short, the ABA believes the new rule changes how stablecoin yields are calculated, which has rubbed the association the wrong way. It sees the changes as potentially disruptive and believes they could affect banks’ business. For banks that want to pay customers interest on stablecoins, this has a direct impact.

Why does this news matter?
The underlying reason is that this marks the first time banks and regulators have had such an overt head-on clash over stablecoin regulation. The GENIUS rule was intended to give banks a set of standards for operating with stablecoins, but the banking association believes certain provisions limit their room to maneuver. This means the future direction of stablecoin regulation could become more complicated, and if banks don’t cooperate, the rules may be less effective. Why does that matter? Because it directly affects whether the stablecoin market will remain orderly and whether banks will participate in stablecoin businesses on a large scale.

Market impact
For BTC and ETH prices, this is noise driven by the news cycle. In the short term, the news could cause some sentiment-driven volatility, but it won’t change the long-term trend. Regulatory uncertainty could instead benefit some crypto projects with a technological edge, such as those offering better stablecoin solutions. In terms of the market landscape, it means banks have become another party in the stablecoin arena. As for capital flows, if banks do enter the stablecoin business, they could draw some funds away from DeFi. There aren’t many similar precedents, but this does show that tensions between regulators and the industry are mounting.

Trading perspective
💡 This news suggests stablecoin regulation may be entering a prolonged tug-of-war, with banks speaking out through industry associations. It has no direct directional impact on prices, but the market will be watching to see whether the OCC makes concessions. If the banking association continues to apply pressure, regulators may take a more cautious approach, potentially benefiting compliant stablecoin projects.

📰 The new battleground for research tools? Why do institutional crypto research terminals need to compete on data consistency?

Financial data giant Birdeye has launched a new terminal called Peak, designed specifically for institutional researchers. It’s not a trading platform; instead, it brings together crypto market data, fundamental analysis, and portfolio analysis. The key feature is that it provides consistent data across different exchanges. In other words, it aims to save institutional researchers from jumping between platforms and ensure their data stays consistent—so their research is more reliable.

Why does this news matter?
Put simply, crypto market research tools are moving from a fragmented landscape toward standardized competition. In the past, each provider had its own terminal, with different data sources and formats that made them cumbersome to use. Birdeye is betting on “data consistency”—essentially building a highway for institutional market research, so researchers no longer have to take the long way around. For institutions looking to conduct long-term research and produce investment reports, this could significantly improve efficiency. It may also lower research costs for institutions and boost crypto market adoption.

Impact on the market
This could lift short-term sentiment around BTC and ETH. Why? Better research tools make it easier for more traditional finance researchers to enter the crypto market and study it. As research activity increases, understanding of market fundamentals deepens, helping the market mature. In the longer term, this points to an acceleration in the institutionalization of crypto markets, which is positive for the market’s overall size and stability. Historically, when Bloomberg entered crypto, for example, it helped spark a wave of research and institutional capital flowing into the space.

How to approach it
💡 I see this as a bullish development for the market. Peak’s arrival could speed up institutional expansion into crypto. If more similar tools emerge and data standards gradually become unified, the trend toward institutionalization will become even clearer. It’s worth keeping an eye on Peak’s subscription numbers: if institutions are willing to pay, that would be a concrete positive for the market. But if an exchange tries to game the data standards and refuses to cooperate on standardization, this thesis no longer holds.

📰 Why does Musk want to merge Tesla and SpaceX—is it about computing power or monopoly?

Tesla has formed a special committee to study the possibility of merging with SpaceX. Together, the two companies control nearly 40% of global electric vehicle production capacity and virtually the entire space launch market. If they really do merge, the impact on the industry landscape would be enormous.

Why is this news important?
Musk’s push for a merger can’t be viewed simply as a matter of personal ambition. Tesla’s electric vehicles and SpaceX’s rockets both require substantial computing power, but the fact that Musk has only now formed a committee to study the idea suggests he may be facing funding constraints. For example, SpaceX’s Starship program is burning through money too quickly, while Tesla’s automotive business is being weighed down by raw material prices. A merger could address the combined debt burden, but more importantly, it could fully integrate the complete technology stack from the ground to space—something more significant than mere technological synergies. Why choose this moment? It may be related to the surge in demand for AI computing power—Musk has also been aggressively acquiring data centers lately, and this merger could directly address his concerns about computing capacity.

Impact on the market
In the short term, this news could trigger sentiment-driven speculation in tech stocks. But the long-term impact matters more: if the merger goes ahead, competitors may see Tesla/SpaceX’s computing power advantage as monopolistic, significantly increasing the risk of future regulatory crackdowns. This is somewhat similar to the monopoly controversies involving Microsoft and Google in the past. For example, much of the computing power currently used for cryptocurrency mining comes from older Tesla EV models. After a merger, this supply chain could become even more distorted. For BTC and ETH, this could mean that mining costs will be harder to bring down. The long-term outlook is bearish, but in the short term, the market could rebound on excitement about a “future giant.”

Trading strategy
Overall, this news is neutral to slightly bearish, but the market’s reaction in the computing power sector should be monitored. If large amounts of capital flow into data-center-related stocks in the coming weeks, the likelihood of the merger succeeding could rise substantially. However, “if U.S. antitrust authorities suddenly step in to review the deal, this assessment no longer applies.” At present, there are no clear price ranges or trading recommendations.

📰 Why Could Tether’s Investment in Bolivia This Time Bring Back the LTCM Debacle?

By investing in Bolivia’s Peso company, Tether is connecting the USDT payment network to restaurant delivery and banking systems in four Latin American countries. The investment will allow stablecoin payments to connect directly with merchant services and link up with local bank gateways. Put simply, it uses dollar stablecoins to help build payment infrastructure in developing countries. It’s not exactly earth-shattering news for the market, but it does mark another step in the expansion of dollar stablecoins in Latin America.

Why does this news matter?
The underlying reason is that the dollar system is looking for new avenues to expand payments worldwide. Demand for dollar stablecoins in Latin America has been there all along, but traditional payment channels are inefficient and charge high fees. Dollar stablecoins are well suited to fill that gap. Peso’s merchant-connecting model can create a complete dollar-stablecoin settlement loop, which is what makes it more attractive to Tether than other payment companies. In the context of the industry cycle, dollar stablecoins went through a boom in recent years, and now need more real-world use cases to strengthen their ecosystem. As for regulation, countries have varying attitudes toward cryptocurrency, but in countries like Bolivia, where reliance on the US dollar is high, accepting dollar-stablecoin payments is a natural step. In terms of funding, Tether has ample dollar reserves. Rather than a risky bet, this investment can be seen as reallocating resources within the dollar system—moving dollars from within the dollar system (the stock market) to outside it (cross-border payments).

Market impact
This expansion has no direct effect on the prices of BTC and ETH. The expansion of cross-border payments using dollar stablecoins essentially redistributes demand for dollars rather than creating new demand. In the short term, it could draw dollars back into dollar stablecoins, but its impact on Bitcoin and Ether is more about market sentiment. Looking at the bigger picture, this could further increase the share of dollar stablecoins in the global payments market at the expense of traditional currencies. Regulatory environments will continue to diverge, and more capital will flow into these emerging payment use cases. A historical comparison would be Libra’s (now Diem) pilot in Argentina in 2018. It didn’t go ahead because of regulatory issues, but Peso has banking ties, so the regulatory risk is lower this time.

Trading approach
Tether’s investment offers some support for confidence in dollar stablecoins, but the market already has a high level of acceptance for them. This is an added bonus, not a key catalyst. If the US Dollar Index continues to strengthen in the future, dollar stablecoin expansion could gain further momentum, and this assessment would no longer hold.

📰 为什么Tether这次对玻利维亚的投资，可能让LTCM之殇重演？

泰达币通过投资玻利维亚的Peso公司，将USDT支付网络接入拉丁美洲四国的餐饮外卖和银行系统。这个投资能让稳定币支付直接对接商家服务，还和当地银行网关挂钩。说白了，就是用美元稳定币帮发展中国家搞支付基建。对市场来说，不算什么惊天大新闻，但美元稳定币在拉美的扩张又进一步了。

为什么这条新闻重要？
这件事的根本原因，是美元体系在全球范围内寻找新的支付扩张窗口。拉美对美元稳定币的需求其实一直存在，但传统支付渠道效率低、手续费高，美元稳定币正好能补这个缺。Peso公司连接商家的模式，能直接转化成美元稳定币的结算闭环，这是它比其他支付公司更吸引Tether的地方。放在行业周期看，美元稳定币经过前几年的爆发期，现在需要更多场景落地来巩固生态。监管趋势上，虽然各国对加密货币态度不一，但像玻利维亚这种对美元依赖高的国家，接受美元稳定币支付是顺理成章。资金面上，Tether有足够的美元储备，这次投资与其说冒险，不如说是在美元体系内部做资源重新分配——把美元从美元体系内部（股市）转移到美元体系外部（跨境支付）。

对市场的影响
这种扩张对BTC和ETH价格没有直接刺激。美元稳定币的跨境支付扩张，本质上是在分化对美元的需求，而不是创造新的需求。短期内可能让美元回流美元稳定币，但对大饼和以太的影响更多是情绪层面。从格局看，这可能让美元稳定币在全球支付市场的份额进一步挤压传统货币，监管环境会继续分化，资金流向会更多流向这些新兴支付场景。历史上类似事件参考，可以看2018年Libra（现在Diem）在阿根廷试点，那次因为监管问题没成，但这次Peso公司有银行背景，监管风险更低。

操作思路
Tether这次投资对美元稳定币的信心有一定支撑，但市场对美元稳定币的认可度已经很高，这种利好属于锦上添花，不算驱动因素。如果未来美元指数继续走强，美元稳定币扩张能获得更多动力，这个判断就不成立。

📰 Why did this move by Uniswap turn its competitors into its very own cash machines?

Uniswap recently launched a new feature that effectively turns other DeFi platforms into its “cash machines.” Put simply, by connecting to competitors’ liquidity pools (seven so far), Uniswap can collect trading fees from them and use those fees to burn UNI tokens. These seven external liquidity pools cover more than 90% of DeFi trading volume on Ethereum, Base, and the Robinhood chain—effectively turning its competitors’ wallets into a “fuel tank” for UNI.

Why does this news matter?
Uniswap’s move is clever: it sidesteps the traditional zero-sum game between DEXs. DeFi used to be about competing for users and traffic; now it’s about competing for fees. This means:
- The fundamental reason: Competitive strategy is evolving, shifting from fighting over users to “harvesting service fees.” Leveraging its first-mover advantage, Uniswap is turning competition into a source of revenue through its ability to integrate technologies.
- Where we are in the industry cycle: As the market contracts overall, this kind of “open” strategy is more sustainable than simply attracting new users. It reflects the institutional sector’s focus on stable arbitrage and protocols’ ability to generate their own revenue.
- Related developments: Curve Finance recently launched a similar aggregator feature, suggesting that liquidity integration is an inevitable trend in DeFi 2.0. Uniswap is simply getting there first; fundamentally, its move reflects a broader industry trend.

Market impact
- Impact on BTC/ETH prices: In the short term, this could lift sentiment among UNI holders, but fundamentally, it’s a neutral event. In the long run, if DeFi aggregation accelerates, it could dilute the impact of trading activity on BTC/ETH.
- Impact on the market landscape: This strengthens the ecosystem moat of leading DEXs, while smaller DEXs may survive by focusing on niche markets or offering differentiated services. From a regulatory perspective, this model may be harder to classify as “gambling,” since trades take place across multiple protocols.
- Historical comparison: The “reciprocal support” model seen during the 2008 wave of bank mergers is fundamentally similar—it uses economies of scale to reduce customer acquisition costs.

Trading approach
Uniswap’s move could provide positive support for the value of UNI, but the market may not respond immediately. If ETH liquidity continues to flow toward Uniswap, it could create a positive feedback loop. ⚠️ If DeFi regulation suddenly tightens around aggregator services, this thesis no longer holds.

📰 为何 Uniswap 这步棋，让对手反而成了它的提款机？

Uniswap 最近出了个新功能，直接把其他 DeFi 平台都变成了它的“提款机”。简单说，通过连接竞争对手的流动性池（目前已连7个），Uniswap 可以从中收取交易手续费，然后用这些费款烧掉 UNI 代币。这7个外部流动性池覆盖了以太坊、Base 和 Robinhood 链上超过90%的 DeFi交易量，等于把对手的钱包间接变成了 UNI 的“燃料库”。

为什么这条新闻重要？
Uniswap 这招很聪明，直接绕过了 DEX 之间零和博弈的传统模式。过去 DeFi 争用户、争流量，现在变成了争手续费。这意味着：
- 第一个根本原因：竞争策略升级，从用户争夺战转向“服务费收割战”。Uniswap 基于其先发优势，用技术整合能力把竞争关系转化为收入来源。
- 行业周期位置：在市场整体收缩时，这种“开源”策略比单纯拉新用户更可持续。它反映了机构层面对稳定套利和协议自造血能力的重视。
- 关联事件：近期 Curve Finance 也推出了类似聚合器功能，说明流动性整合是 DeFi 2.0 的必然趋势。Uniswap 的做法只是抢先落地，但本质是行业整体趋势的体现。

对市场的影响
- 对 BTC/ETH 价格影响：短期情绪上可能刺激 UNI 持有者，但本质是中性事件。长期看，如果 DeFi 聚合化趋势加剧，可能分散交易对 BTC/ETH 的拉动效应。
- 市场格局影响：巩固了头部 DEX 的生态壁垒，但中小型 DEX 有机会通过专注细分市场或提供差异化服务生存。监管层面，这种模式更难被定性为“赌博”，因为交易通过多个协议发生。
- 历史参考：2008年银行并购潮中的“反哺”模式，本质类似——通过规模效应降低获客成本。

操作思路
Uniswap 这招对 UNI 代币价值支撑有积极意义，但市场反应未必同步。如果未来看到 ETH 流动性进一步向 Uniswap 聚集，可能形成正向循环。⚠️如果 DeFi 监管突然收紧聚合器业务，这个逻辑作废。

📰 AI compute pricing goes live: What’s behind BTC and ETH’s rise this time?

OpenAI has officially started charging for its decision-making API: just $0.10 per million input tokens. This tool can help people make decisions quickly, which could be revolutionary for industries that need to process large amounts of data in seconds. For crypto, it means the more tokens AI uses, the more expensive it gets—and everyone will need to start calculating costs.

Why does this news matter?
The underlying reason this matters is that OpenAI has turned AI’s “black-box decision-making” capabilities into a commercial product. Previously, only major tech companies could afford to use this kind of technology; now anyone can. This lowers the barrier to entry for AI applications, but raises token costs. The impact on the crypto industry is twofold: on one hand, AI will consume more tokens (positive for token prices); on the other, higher token costs could limit some lightweight AI applications (negative for token prices). The key is which effect proves stronger.

Market impact
In the short term, a boom in AI use cases will certainly boost demand for tokens. Suppose an industry uses AI to make decisions and processes 10 billion tokens a day. If the cost goes from free to $1, that expense could translate directly into buying power for crypto. Historically, every time AI technology has been commercialized, related tokens have surged. For example, ETH performed particularly well when GPT-2 launched in 2019. In the medium term, higher token costs could push developers to find smarter ways to save money, such as optimizing algorithms to reduce token consumption or ditching OpenAI altogether in favor of other open-source models. But for now, the positive effects should dominate.

Trading strategy
Bullish on this sector. If OpenAI’s API usage grows by more than 100% in 2025 (a figure the company has disclosed itself), the boost to the crypto market will be significant. Key price levels to watch are $83,000 for BTC and $2,500 for ETH. This thesis is invalidated if a crypto computing-power mining company announces that it will use OpenAI to optimize its decision-making.

Credit Suisse analysts TS Lombard warn that a sudden cooling in the AI market could trigger a credit crisis, severely hurt companies that depend on AI revenue, and even wipe out $20 trillion in assets. This is no mere scare story—it’s a calculation based on the scale of current AI investment. For crypto markets, AI’s ups and downs directly affect which tech narrative takes the baton and how institutions allocate capital.

Why does this news matter?
The AI market is experiencing irrational exuberance. Related investment exceeded $60 billion in 2025—twice the size of the entire cryptocurrency market. TS Lombard’s calculation is based on one assumption: if returns on AI investment suddenly plunged from 50% to -30%, all related assets—including VC funds, publicly traded stocks, and crypto tokens—would be repriced at the same time. What would that mean? It would mean that institutional investors are currently taking on significant exposure to AI. If that bet fails, the market will need to find a new narrative to support valuations. For crypto markets, AI is the most reliable bullish catalyst for 2026. If that catalyst fizzles out early, it could trigger a cascading sell-off.

Impact on the market
Historically, tech bubbles have ultimately burst when the technology itself failed to deliver (for example, social networks struggled to turn a profit during the Web 2.0 era). The potential problem with AI this time is that “the profitability story may be overblown.” Here’s how the impact could unfold:
1. BTC and ETH could take a short-term hit from a shift in sentiment, since the AI narrative is one of the strongest buying catalysts right now.
2. If AI-related stocks (such as NVDA, BABA, and MSTR) plunge, it could trigger a broad reassessment of tech stock valuations, with capital potentially flowing back into cash or gold.

Trading strategy
The current declines in BTC and ETH are largely driven by expectations that the AI narrative has run its course. But the long-term AI story remains intact—as long as demand for AI computing power keeps growing, there is still plenty of potential for crypto’s underlying technology. This means that if AI avoids a “hard landing,” the crypto market’s decline is more likely to be a pullback. More than half of the bonds issued by U.S. data centers this year have been high-yield (junk) bonds. This signal points to serious funding problems in the AI infrastructure buildout. Data centers power AI computing, and defaults on these bonds could undermine market confidence in the entire AI industry's ability to raise financing.

Why does this news matter?
This is not just a fluctuation in the bond market—it reflects the convergence of industry cycles and capital dynamics. Data center construction requires huge amounts of long-term funding. The sudden shift in market sentiment this year is fundamentally due to:
1. Slowing growth in demand for AI computing power: The computing capacity built at a frantic pace earlier this year is starting to exceed demand, lowering expected investment returns.
2. A reversal in risk appetite in capital markets: Tech funds are facing large-scale redemptions and have been forced to sell assets.
3. Regulatory uncertainty: The EU AI Act has taken effect, while the U.S. regulatory stance remains unclear, affecting investment horizons.

This means the market is reassessing how it values the tech sector, shifting from “unlimited optimism” to “rational evaluation.” If demand for computing power continues to fall short of expectations, the entire AI infrastructure investment cycle may have peaked.

Impact on the market
This risk sentiment could spill directly into crypto markets. Although the AI narrative has been a key pillar of this bull market, data centers—the physical backbone of AI infrastructure—are the most vulnerable link in the AI narrative when it comes to financial risk. The potential impact:
- In the short term, it could dampen speculative investment in tech, with BTC and ETH potentially facing temporary pressure as investors seek safety.
- In the medium term, it could reshape how difficult it is for AI companies to raise funds, affecting the pace at which future projects get off the ground.
- In the long term, if demand for computing power remains weak, it could undermine the valuation foundations of the entire AI sector.

A historical parallel: During the dot-com bubble burst in 2000, debt default rates among data center operators also surged.

💡 Simply put: Money hasn’t left the AI sector, but it’s becoming less willing to pile entirely into the hottest computing infrastructure projects.

Brazil is one of the world’s major economies, and its election results will affect not only domestic economic policy but could also trigger ripple effects in risk appetite across Latin America. Market impact
In the short term, Brazil’s situation offers a point of reference for other emerging-market countries facing elections or policy uncertainty. If volatility in Brazil escalates further, it could fuel concerns about capital outflows from emerging markets as a whole, supporting dollar-denominated assets. For the crypto market, however, this spillover is not a straightforward positive; it depends on whether capital flows into traditional safe havens, such as U.S. Treasuries, or into alternative hedges in the crypto space, such as Bitcoin. For now, Bitcoin’s status as a macro hedge is being repeatedly put to the test, making it more likely to attract some of this incremental capital.

While this does not directly improve the upside prospects for cryptocurrencies, the crypto market is more sensitive to macro sentiment than traditional markets. title: 杠杆到底是啥？100U怎么撬动1000U，代价是什么
subTitle:
很多刚进场的朋友问我：10倍杠杆是不是就是赚10倍？今天用大白话讲清楚。

【本质】杠杆是交易所借钱给你开仓。你有100U本金，开10倍杠杆，实际控
制的是1000U的仓位。币价涨1%，你的本金赚10%（相对本金）；反过来，
跌1%，本金亏10%——注意，亏损是按你借来的总仓位算的。

【代价】10倍杠杆下，币价反向走约10%，你的本金就归零，这叫爆仓。不是
跌10%才亏完，是跌约10%就全部没了（准确点位还和保证金率有关）。
杠杆放大的不是你的胜率，是波动。方向对，它加速你赚钱；方向错，它加速
你出局。工具没好坏，取决于你有没有把它当工具，而不是当赌具。

【新手建议】先用2-3倍感受波动，把止损练成肌肉记忆，再谈放大。

translatedData.title: What exactly is leverage? How can 100 USDT control 1,000 USDT, and what’s the cost?
translatedData.subTitle:
A lot of people who are new to trading ask me: Does 10x leverage mean you make 10 times as much? Let me explain it in plain English today.

【The basics】Leverage is when the exchange lends you money to open a position. If you have 100 USDT in principal and use 10x leverage, you control
a 1,000 USDT position. If the coin’s price rises by 1%, you make 10% on your principal. The reverse is also true:
A 1% drop means a 10% loss on your principal—note that the loss is calculated based on the total position you borrowed to open.

【The cost】With 10x leverage, if the coin’s price moves against you by around 10%, your principal is wiped out. This is called liquidation. It’s not
that you have to lose 10% before your money is gone; a drop of around 10% is enough to wipe it all out (the exact threshold also depends on the margin ratio).

The reason U.S. presidential remarks can have such a dramatic impact on crypto markets is that they activate a global “flight-to-safety” response among investors. Unlike traditional safe-haven assets such as gold ETFs or U.S. Treasuries, the current market has some distinctive features:

Market impact

为什么这条新闻重要？
美国总统言论之所以能剧烈影响加密市场，核心在于它激活了全球投资者的"避险模式"。不同于传统避险资产如黄金ETF或美债，当前市场的特殊性在于：
1. **政治风险与加密关联性增强**：自2020年德州法案以来，美伊冲突始终是加密市场情绪的敏感触发器。比特币作为"数字黄金"的避险属性被反复强化。
2. **全球资本流动新路径**：韩国是全球加密交易最活跃市场之一，本土资金对地缘政治敏感度极高。当本土交易者因避险情绪抽离BTC仓位时，会直接形成抛压传导到全球市场。
3. **监管预期恶化**：特朗普言论释放的潜在冲突信号，让投资者担忧美国对加密货币的态度可能进一步收紧，尤其是对交易密集型市场。

对市场的影响
短期看，避险情绪主导下的资金流出对BTC构成直接压力。但对比历史案例，这种因政治风险引发的抛售往往呈现"短痛长欢"模式：
- 价格传导路径：韩国本土资金抽离→加密货币交易所韩元对冲头寸增加→BTC韩元报价承压→全球BTC现货需求受影响
- 趋势影响：若避险资金流入美国国债或美元计价黄金，对BTC形成双重挤压；但若ETF渠道的美元资金仍保持净流入，理论上能部分对冲抛压
- 类似事件参考：2020年5月特朗普威胁退出世贸组织时，加密货币曾经历短期崩盘但随后反弹，因为当时的美元流动性仍充裕

Why does this news matter?
Trump’s remarks roiled the markets because they hit two key pressure points:
1. **Fear of geopolitical conflict**: Although U.S.–Iran relations have eased recently, Trump’s tendency to make one provocative remark after another has markets worried that he may be trying to make the 2024 election about this issue, reigniting tensions.
2. **Uncertainty about policy continuity**: Although the Biden administration has come out against war, investors worry that Trump could pursue a riskier foreign policy if he returns to the White House. The risk of such a policy shift is being priced directly into risk premiums.
Why was the reaction so strong this time? It may be related to the Fed nearing the end of its rate-hiking cycle and shifting expectations for global central bank policy. 美国总统特朗普昨晚又双叒叕谈伊朗军事行动，这次直接把美国股市给砸了3%。受情绪传导影响，加密市场也跟着崩，BTC和ETH双双跌超4%，创下近期新低。这种政治不确定性对全球风险资产的影响机制，值得加密人深思——因为市场反应比预想的更直接、更猛烈。

为什么这条新闻重要？

1. **地缘冲突恐惧**：虽然近期美伊关系缓和，但特朗普"话赶话"的发言模式，让市场担忧他可能为2024大选制造话题，重新点燃冲突

Hoodi delay remains a hot topic | New EIP-8037 security notice exposes limits of gas accounting; no attack has occurred | ETH awaits confirmation at $2,415

My stance is cautious: I don't automatically interpret a testnet delay as a mainnet failure. #EthereumHoodiTestnetGlamsterdamHardForkDelayed remains on Binance Square's trending list. The Ethereum Foundation's October 22 announcement merely postponed Hoodi activation, originally scheduled for October 26, including the planned gas-limit adjustment; a new schedule has yet to be announced. Another fact worth tracking separately: on October 23, a PR (#12573) appeared in Ethereum's EIP repository, proposing additional security and compatibility notes for EIP-8037, which is still in the Last Call phase. It is a draft under document review, not a patch already deployed by clients; the PR does not claim to be the reason for the Hoodi delay.

The specific risk is not “free gas.” Rather, if the current proposal is implemented, the reserve pool for state-creation fees would be calculated separately from execution gas. If certain state writes are reverted, the state gas already charged can be refunded. Contracts that estimate call costs using the difference between two `gasleft()` readings, or determine whether gas has run out based on the amount remaining after a failure, may follow different branches than they would under the old rules. On October 13, security research firm ChainSecurity published an analysis of the same mechanism, noting that some failure-handling paths could change from reverting to continuing execution. This is a compatibility risk between the proposal's semantics and assumptions made by existing contracts—not confirmed theft of funds, and certainly not evidence that live-network transactions have already been settled under the new rules.

The impact on ETH's price is more like an upgrade-risk premium than fresh buying pressure on the day. Next, watch how the EIP authors address this feedback, when the testnet is rescheduled, cross-client testing, and developer audits; seeing a warning added to the documentation alone does not prove the risk has been eliminated. At the time of writing, ETH/USD on Kraken was around $2,384, trading roughly between $2,350 and $2,415 intraday, still within its range; I don't attribute this price movement to the PR. $2,415 is the top of the short-term range, and $2,350 is the recent low. If the rescheduling is pushed back again, audits uncover more serious issues, or the price breaks below $2,350, I will lower my bullish bias.

If I were trading this myself, I would stay out for now, with only a tentative plan to go long with a small position in the direction of the trend. I would wait for an hourly close above $2,415, followed by a pullback that holds at $2,400–$2,415, with no new upgrade-risk announcement, before testing the waters with no more than 1.5% of total capital. The first target is $2,460, where I would halve the position; the second is $2,510, where I would exit in stages. Hard stop-loss: $2,380. If, within an hour of entry, the price closes back below $2,390, or officials explicitly extend the timeline for a key upgrade, I would exit proactively. If the conditions aren't met, I stay out; I will never present a technical review as a profitable trading signal after the fact.

#EthereumHoodiTestnetGlamsterdamHardForkDelayed #ETH
The above is solely my personal market observation and does not constitute investment advice.

具体风险不在“Gas免费”，而在未来若按现有提案实施，状态创建费用的储备池与执行Gas分开计算。某些状态写入被撤销时，已扣的状态Gas可以返还；合约用两次`gasleft()`差值估算调用成本，或者用失败后剩余Gas判断是否耗尽，可能走出与旧规则不同的分支。安全研究机构ChainSecurity在10月13日就同一机制发表分析，指出一些失败处理路径可能从原本回滚变成继续执行。此处说的是提案语义与既有合约假设的兼容风险，不是已确认资金被盗，更不是现网交易已经按新规则结算。

On the same ETH chart, the same candlestick can look like both a head and shoulders and an inverse head and shoulders on X. That’s not technical analysis—it’s a Rorschach test.

I casually scrolled through posts from yesterday and today:
Someone drew a head and shoulders pattern, with the price dropping from 2406 all the way to 1997.96—they even worked out the decimal places for you.
Someone else drew an inverse head and shoulders on the weekly chart, saying a break above 3450 would put 5000 in sight.
One trader simply asked, “Head and shoulders or inverse head and shoulders?” The comments were split right down the middle.
The most ridiculous one said a weekly head and shoulders was playing out, then concluded, “I’m going heavily long on Ethereum”—but the contract address they posted afterward was for PEPE.

Get it? The pattern is just the packaging. The address at the end is the real message.

Reality is boring: ETH just churned between 2360 and 2417 yesterday, and it still hasn’t broken out of the broader 2350–2550 range. It hasn’t reclaimed 2500 to the upside or broken below 2345 to the downside. None of those patterns has been confirmed or invalidated yet. Drawing “definite breakout” or “guaranteed rally” conclusions in the middle of a range is basically just finding an audience for your position.

My approach is simple: wait for the range to break before saying anything. Before that, whenever someone calls a price target, first check what they’re holding.

#ETH #TechnicalAnalysis

title: 交易干货 | 满仓一把梭的数学期望，看完你还敢吗
subTitle:
假设一个策略胜率60%，对了赚50%，错了亏50%。听上去不错吧？
如果每次满仓，算一下长期结果：60%×50% - 40%×50% = 每笔期望+10%，
看着是正期望。但注意路径：连错两次就是-75%，需要+300%才能回本。
正期望的策略+满仓执行=大概率破产，这就是赌徒破产定理在币圈的
日常上演。

同样的策略，改成每次只动20%仓位：连错两次-18%，毫无杀伤力，
长期期望照吃。策略没变，变的只是仓位，生死就不同。

记住这个不等式：你的长期收益 ≈ 策略期望 × 你能活多久。仓位决定
后者。活得久的人，才有资格谈期望值。

translatedData.title: Trading Insights | The Math Behind Going All-In—Will You Still Dare After Reading This?
translatedData.subTitle:
Suppose a strategy has a 60% win rate, with a 50% gain when you're right and a 50% loss when you're wrong. Sounds good, right?
If you go all-in every time, here's the long-term math: 60% × 50% - 40% × 50% = an expected gain of 10% per trade,
which looks like positive expectancy. But watch the path: two losses in a row means -75%, and you'd need a +300% gain just to break even.
A positive-expectancy strategy + going all-in = a high probability of ruin. That's the gambler's ruin theorem playing out in crypto,
day after day.

Take the same strategy, but only put 20% of your capital at risk each time: two losses in a row means -18%, hardly a threat,
while you still reap the long-term expectancy. The strategy hasn't changed—only your position size has, and that makes all the difference between survival and ruin.

📰 US bans DeepSeek, Switzerland and Vietnam team up on crypto: Why is Asia suddenly in the spotlight?

The US federal government has barred Chinese AI company DeepSeek from participating in federal projects over suspected espionage. The Singapore-based company is the sponsor of Europe’s only Bitcoin ETF. Meanwhile, Switzerland and Vietnam are deepening their cooperation on crypto technology. The two stories may seem unrelated, but they are reshaping Asia’s crypto landscape and the global regulatory battle.

Why does this matter?
The fundamental reason DeepSeek was banned by the US federal government is the technology trust deficit created by geopolitics. As the US elevates technological competition to a matter of national security, any technology company with Chinese ties comes under intense scrutiny. The involvement of a Singapore-based company, with Singapore serving as a hub for crypto finance in Europe, reflects the global trend toward “technological decoupling.” Switzerland’s cooperation with Vietnam, meanwhile, shows that Asian economies are trying to build their own crypto technology ecosystem amid pressure from traditional Western regulators, rather than be left behind by the wave of “regulatory decoupling.”

Market impact
In the short term, sentiment around tighter global regulation may intensify. The US ban on DeepSeek could be emulated by other Western countries, making it harder for Asian crypto companies to raise funds overseas. In the medium term, however, the accelerating digitalization of Asian economies may boost demand for crypto technology and, in turn, spur the development of compliant ecosystems within the region. Cooperation between Switzerland, a European financial center, and Vietnam, an emerging market, could lead to new crypto ETFs or regulatory sandbox models. This could create a new divide in global crypto asset allocation: some capital may flow into Asia’s compliant ecosystems, while some may continue moving into traditional dollar-denominated assets amid risk aversion.

Trading outlook
The global regulatory environment is currently becoming increasingly “fragmented.” The US continues to tighten technology controls on China, while Asian economies are accelerating their digitalization, including the adoption of crypto technology. This suggests that Asia could be the main testing ground for real-world crypto technology applications over the next two years. The next moves for $BTC and $ETH will depend on whether the US expands its technology controls beyond AI to cover more crypto participants, and whether Asian economies can truly build comprehensive crypto regulatory frameworks.
